name: AKASA vs Waystar Eligibility
title: AKASA vs Waystar: AI RCM Automation Compared
description: Compare AKASA (AI RCM automation for Epic, 80-90% automation) vs Waystar Eligibility (90M+ monthly transactions, broad EHR support). Enterprise revenue cycle platforms.

summary.bottom_line: AKASA and Waystar are both enterprise RCM solutions but with different focuses. AKASA uses AI and human expertise for deep automation (80-90% of routine tasks) with primary focus on Epic environments. Waystar Eligibility processes 90M+ transactions monthly with broad EHR support (Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, NextGen). Choose based on EHR ecosystem and automation depth needs.

key_differences.approach: AKASA: AI + human experts | Waystar: Platform + AI
key_differences.ehr_focus: AKASA: Epic primary | Waystar: Broad support
key_differences.automation: AKASA: 80-90% routine tasks | Waystar: Intelligent alerts

rows.entity_a: Epic health systems wanting deep automation

sections.heading: Enterprise RCM Approaches
sections.content: AKASA and Waystar represent different approaches to enterprise RCM. AKASA uses 'Unified Automation' - AI that learns from human experts to handle routine tasks with human-level accuracy, achieving 80-90% automation. It's deeply integrated with Epic. Waystar Eligibility is a broader platform processing 90M+ transactions monthly across many EHRs, using AI for intelligent alerts and denial prevention rather than full task automation.

sections.heading: Automation Depth
sections.content: AKASA automates end-to-end workflows: prior authorization submission/tracking/appeals, claims status checks, payment posting, and denial management. The AI handles exceptions that break traditional RPA bots. Waystar Eligibility focuses on real-time verification with proactive alerts for coverage gaps and out-of-network risks - it prevents problems rather than automating full workflows.

sections.heading: Investment Comparison
sections.content: Both require enterprise contracts. AKASA uses ROI-based pricing with proof-of-concept pilots for qualified health systems. Waystar ranges from $100-300/provider/month for small practices to $2,000-5,000+/month for mid-sized organizations, with implementation costs of $2,000-10,000+. Neither publishes transparent pricing - quotes required.

recommendations.when: You're an Epic health system wanting to automate 80-90% of routine RCM tasks with AI that handles exceptions.
You need broad EHR support (Epic + Cerner + athenahealth + others) for eligibility verification at scale.
Prior authorization volume is overwhelming your team and you want end-to-end automation.
You need denial prevention through upfront verification rather than full workflow automation.

faqs.q: Does AKASA work with non-Epic EHRs?
faqs.a: AKASA supports Cerner/Oracle Health but Epic is their primary focus with the deepest integration. Non-Epic environments may have limited automation capabilities.

AKASA combines AI/ML with human expertise rather than pure RPA. The AI learns from human experts and can handle exceptions that break traditional bots, achieving human-level accuracy with automation efficiency.
Waystar Eligibility is one module in Waystar's broader RCM platform. Waystar also offers claims management, denial management, and prior authorization products that can be added.

faqs.q: Which is better for small practices?
faqs.a: Neither. Both are enterprise solutions. Small practices should consider Tebra, Candid Health, or other solutions designed for their scale.
